source.title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems

accepted.question_text: Let P_α(z) = exp(2πiα)z + z², where α is an irrational Bruno number, and let S_α be the maximal connected open neighborhood of 0 on which P_α is analytically linearizable. Does there exist such an α for which the boundary ∂S_α is a C¹ submanifold of the complex plane, equivalently a circle?

evidence.quote: Does there exist α1 a Bruno number such that ∂Sα1 (the boundary of Sα1) is a C1 submanifold of C (a circle) ?

accepted.question_text: For the same quadratic polynomial P_α(z) = exp(2πiα)z + z² with α a Bruno irrational and S_α its maximal Siegel singular disk, does there exist such an α for which the boundary ∂S_α is not a Jordan curve?

evidence.quote: Does there exist α2 a Bruno number such that ∂Sα2 (the boundary of Sα2) is not a Jordan curve ?

accepted.question_text: Fix a Diophantine vector α in T^n. Let U_α be the set of smooth zero-average functions φ on T^n such that the exact symplectic map F_φ(θ,r) = (θ + r, r + ∂φ/∂θ(θ + r)) preserves an invariant torus graph on which F_φ is smoothly conjugate to the translation R_α: θ ↦ θ + α. Is the boundary ∂U_α, viewed in the smooth function space C^∞(T^n), locally a C^k submanifold for some finite k ≥ 0?

evidence.quote: Is the boundary ∂Uα of Uα in C∞(Tn) a locally flat Ck-submanifold (for some k ≥ 0) ?

accepted.question_text: In the same setting for U_α, is every boundary point x ∈ ∂U_α accessible both from within U_α and from the complement of U_α?

evidence.quote: Nothing is known (e.g. is every point x ∈ ∂Uα accessible from Uα and the exterior of Uα ?).

accepted.question_text: Let U = ⋃_{α ∈ DC} U_α, where U_α is the class of perturbation potentials whose associated exact symplectic map preserves a smooth invariant torus with Diophantine translation vector α. What is the smallest real number k for which U is open near 0 in the C^k topology?

evidence.quote: Let ⋃α∈DC Uα = U ; what is the minimal number k ∈ R+ for which U is open near 0, in the Ck-topology ?

accepted.question_text: When n = 1 and α is of constant type, it is known that U_α is open near 0 in the Sobolev topology W^{4,p} for p > 1. Does the same openness statement remain true for p = 1, i.e. in W^{4,1}?

evidence.quote: The author has been unable to decide if this is also true when p = 1 !

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a real-analytic diffeomorphism of either the annulus T¹ × [-1,1] or the sphere S² that is homotopic to the identity, preserves Lebesgue measure, has only finitely many periodic orbits, and nevertheless has a dense orbit?

evidence.quote: Does there exist a Cω (= R-analytic)-diffeomorphism, homotopic to the identity, Lebesgue measure-preserving, of T1×[-1, 1] or S2, with a finite number of periodic orbits and a dense orbit ?

accepted.question_text: Let f be a C^∞ diffeomorphism of the annulus T¹ × [-1,1] that preserves Lebesgue measure, is homotopic to the identity, has only finitely many periodic points, and whose boundary rotation number α is Diophantine. Must f be C^∞-conjugate to the rigid annulus translation R_α(θ,r) = (θ + α, r)?

evidence.quote: Is f C∞-conjugated to Rα(θ; r) = (θ + α; r) ?

accepted.question_text: Let f be a Lebesgue-measure-preserving smooth diffeomorphism of the closed disk D² with only finitely many periodic points. Must f be C^∞-conjugate to the rigid rotation r_α(z) = exp(2πiα) z for a suitable angle α?

evidence.quote: When f is Lebesgue measure preserving and f has a finite number of periodic points is f C∞-conjugated to rα ?

accepted.question_text: Let f be a germ of a real-analytic symplectic diffeomorphism of R^{2n} fixing the origin, with linear part conjugate in Sp(2n,R) to a product of planar rotations with Diophantine frequency vector α. Must every sufficiently small neighborhood of 0 contain a positive-Lebesgue-measure set of invariant Lagrangian tori for f?

evidence.quote: If f is real analytic, then f leaves invariant, in any small neighbourhood of 0, a set of positive Lebesgue measure of Lagrangian tori .

accepted.question_text: Let G^1_μ(D²) be the C¹ compactly supported Lebesgue-measure-preserving diffeomorphisms of the disk. Does every C¹-neighborhood of the identity in G^1_μ(D²) contain some map g with positive metric entropy h_μ(g) > 0?

evidence.quote: For every C1-neighbourhood W of the identity in G1μ there exists g ∈ W such that hμ(g) > 0.

accepted.question_text: For G^1_μ(D²), let G be the set of maps f with λ⁺(f,μ) = 0, where λ⁺ is the maximal integrated Lyapunov exponent. Which of the following two mutually exclusive alternatives holds: (a) G is a dense G_δ subset, or (b) there exists a nonempty C¹-open set U and a constant δ > 0 such that every g in U satisfies h_μ(g) ≥ δ?

evidence.quote: Question. Is a) or b) true ?

accepted.question_text: Let G^1_ψ(M) denote either the C¹ smooth-measure-preserving or the C¹ symplectic diffeomorphisms of a compact manifold M, and let SE^1_ψ be the class of maps that remain uniformly positive in maximal Lyapunov exponent on all nearby periodic-orbit measures under small C¹ perturbations. Is the subset of maps in G^1_ψ(M) that admit a dominated splitting on all of M C¹-dense inside SE^1_ψ?

evidence.quote: Is the set {f ∈ G1ψ(M); f has a dominated splitting on M} C1-dense in SE1ψ ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a connected simply connected manifold M^n that admits a partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism?

evidence.quote: Does there exist a connected and simply connected manifold Mn with a partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism ?

accepted.question_text: On the complement G^1_ψ(M) \ SE^1_ψ, which side of the entropy dichotomy analogous to Question 4.3 holds: generic zero maximal Lyapunov exponent, or instead a nonempty open region of uniformly positive entropy?

evidence.quote: On G1ψ(M) \ SE1ψ, which of the two possibilities of 4.3 is true ?

accepted.question_text: If f is a strictly ergodic C¹ diffeomorphism of a compact connected manifold, meaning that f is both minimal and uniquely ergodic, must its topological entropy be equal to 0?

evidence.quote: Conjecture. The topological entropy of f equals 0.

accepted.question_text: Let G be the set of C^∞ diffeomorphisms of T^n isotopic to the identity that have no periodic points, and let Ḡ be its closure in the C^∞ topology. For n ≥ 2, does Ḡ have empty interior in Diff^∞_0(T^n)?
accepted.context_brief: Periodic-point closing problem on the torus

evidence.quote: Question. Does the closed set G have no interior (n ≥ 2) in Diff∞0(Tn) ?

accepted.question_text: Let H₀(r) be a real-analytic strictly convex superlinear Hamiltonian on T^n × R^n with ∂H₀/∂r(0) = 0 and n ≥ 2. Can one find a real-analytic one-parameter perturbation H_ε(θ,r) = H₀(r) + εH′(θ,r,ε) and some small ε₀ such that, on the energy surface H_{ε₀}^{-1}(1), the periodic orbits of the Hamiltonian flow are not dense?
accepted.context_brief: Sparse periodic orbits in convex Hamiltonian dynamics

evidence.quote: Question. Can one find a Cω-family Hε(θ; r) = H0(r)+εH′0(θ; r; ε) ... such that for some ε0 small on H−1ε0(1), the periodic orbits of the Hamiltonian flow of Hε0 are not dense ?

accepted.question_text: For n ≥ 2, does there exist a smooth compact connected hypersurface M^{2n−1} in R^{2n} whose characteristic flow is minimal, meaning that every orbit is dense in M^{2n−1}?

evidence.quote: When n ≥ 2 can one find M2n−1 ⊂ R2n, a C∞-compact connected hypersurface, such that on M2n−1 the characteristic flow is minimal (every orbit is dense) ?

accepted.question_text: Can the characteristic flow on a smooth compact connected hypersurface M^{2n−1} ⊂ R^{2n} be an Anosov flow?

evidence.quote: Can the characteristic flow on M2n−1 be an Anosov flow ?

accepted.question_text: Let M^n be a compact connected oriented manifold of dimension n ≥ 3 with Euler characteristic 0, equipped with a smooth volume form, and consider nowhere-zero divergence-free vector fields on M^n. In every homotopy class of such nowhere-zero vector fields, does there exist one whose flow has no periodic orbit?

evidence.quote: Does there exist vector fields as above (in every homotopy class of non-zero vector fields) such that the flow of fXt has no periodic orbit ?

accepted.question_text: In the same setting of nowhere-zero divergence-free vector fields on a compact connected oriented manifold M^n with n ≥ 3 and Euler characteristic 0, does there exist such a vector field whose flow is volume-ergodic?

evidence.quote: Does there exist vector-fields as above such that the flow fXt is μ-ergodic ?

accepted.question_text: Let (M^{2n}, ω) be a compact symplectic manifold with Euler characteristic 0 that does not fiber over S¹. Must every symplectic diffeomorphism of M^{2n} that is homotopic to the identity have a fixed point? More strongly, must it have at least as many fixed points as the minimal number of zeros of any symplectic vector field on M^{2n}?
accepted.context_brief: Fixed points on symplectic manifolds with χ=0

evidence.quote: Conjecture. Every symplectic diffeomorphism homotopic to the identity of (M2n; ω), where χ(M2n) = 0 and M2n does not fiber over S1, has a fixed point (in fact a number of fixed points ≥ minimal number of zeros of any symplectic vector-field).

accepted.question_text: For n ≥ 3, can one find a smooth Hamiltonian H in a small C^k neighborhood, with k ≥ 2, of the integrable Hamiltonian H₀(r) = 1/2‖r‖² on T^n × R^n such that the Hamiltonian flow on the energy surface H^{-1}(1) has at least one dense orbit?

evidence.quote: Can one find an example of a C∞-Hamiltonian H in a small Ck-neighbourhood k ≥ 2 of H0(r) = 1/2‖r‖2 such that, on H−1(1), the Hamiltonian flow of H has one dense orbit ?

accepted.question_text: For a generic smooth Hamiltonian H near the convex integrable model H₀ and a generic ergodic minimizing Mather measure μ, is the restricted flow f_t^H on supp(μ) hyperbolic?

evidence.quote: For the C∞-generic H and the generic ergodic minimal measure μ of Mather, is the flow fHt|supp(μ) on H−1(1) a hyperbolic flow ?

accepted.question_text: For a generic smooth Hamiltonian H on the energy surface H^{-1}(1), are the invariant probability measures supported on periodic orbits dense, in the weak topology, in the set of ergodic minimizing measures?

evidence.quote: For the C∞-generic H on H−1(1) are the probability measures defined by periodic orbits, dense (in the weak topology on probability measures) in the ergodic minimal measures ?

accepted.question_text: Can one generically find a closed connected invariant set F inside H^{-1}(1) that contains all supports of ergodic minimizing measures, has the property that orbits asymptotic to locally minimizing orbits are dense in F, and for which the restricted Hamiltonian flow on F has a dense orbit?
accepted.context_brief: Large invariant set containing Mather dynamics

evidence.quote: Can one find C∞-generically a closed connected set F, invariant by the Hamiltonian flow fHt of H, F ⊂ H−1(1), such that F contains all the supports of the ergodic minimal measures, in F the orbits asymptotic to the locally minimal orbits are dense in F, and on F, fHt|F has a dense orbit ?

accepted.question_text: Consider the spatial n-body problem with n ≥ 3, after fixing the center of mass and reparametrizing the flow on each energy surface so that the new Hamiltonian flow of H_e is complete on H_e^{-1}(0). For every energy e, is the nonwandering set of this flow nowhere dense in H_e^{-1}(0)?
accepted.context_brief: Topological instability in the n-body problem

evidence.quote: Question. Is for every e the non wandering set of the Hamiltonian flow of He on H−1e (0) nowhere dense in H−1e (0) ?

accepted.question_text: In the spatial n-body problem with one mass m₀ = 1 and the remaining masses m_j = εM_j for 1 ≤ j ≤ n−1, with all M_j > 0 and ε small, does every neighborhood of distinct coplanar circular orbits around m₀ moving in the same direction contain wandering domains?
accepted.context_brief: Wandering domains in a small-mass n-body regime

evidence.quote: when ε is small, there are wandering domains .
